description: Hi, I'm Michał. I'm a Computer Science student at Rzeszów University of Technology. I specialize in seamlessly bridging hardware and software—my tech stack includes Python (PyTorch, FastAPI, OpenCV), Flutter for mobile/desktop apps, databases (PostgreSQL, Supabase), and IoT (Raspberry Pi, ESP32, RFID).
summary: I developed ARES-HUD, an interactive dual-mode mapping application featuring a Habitat Planning Console and a first-person Spacesuit Visor AR HUD.   It addresses the challenge by fusing five NASA datasets: HiRISE, CRISM, THEMIS, RAD, and RIMFAX into a hyper-localized tactical map. Astronauts can overlay topography, spectral mineralogy, thermal inertia, and radiation data to plan safe, metabolic-efficient EVA routes using our A* pathfinder. The tool guides crews to critical science targets, like Mount Sharp's boxwork formations, while displaying simulated rover ground-truth perspectives.   This is important because while current NASA tools excel at global mapping, astronauts require meter-by-meter intelligence to survive on the ground. Operating under strict metabolic and mobility constraints, crews need real-time situational awareness. ARES-HUD ensures safety by helping astronauts avoid dust traps, tracking life-support consumables, and instantly vectoring crews to natural cliff shelters during sudden Solar Particle Events (SPEs), bridging the gap between orbital data and safe human exploration.
details: ARES-HUD is an interactive, hyper-localized mapping platform designed for the first human explorers on Mars, bridging the critical gap between global orbital maps and meter-by-meter tactical survival. It operates through two synchronized interfaces: a Habitat Tactical Console for pre-EVA planning and a first-person Spacesuit Visor AR HUD for real-time surface navigation. By fusing five NASA datasets (HiRISE, CRISM, THEMIS, RAD, and RIMFAX), our custom A* pathfinding algorithm calculates the safest, most metabolic-efficient routes. It actively prevents astronauts from sinking by penalizing low-thermal-inertia dust traps and avoids steep slopes that hazard xEMU suits. The tool maximizes both safety and scientific return, guiding crews to authentic astrobiological targets like Mount Sharp's boxwork formations. We creatively translated geological data into dynamic survival mechanics—for instance, triggering a simulated Solar Particle Event (SPE) instantly aborts the mission and vectors the crew to a natural cliff alcove based on topographic shielding. Considering the severe physical limitations of Marswalks, we also integrated a toggle for a HEX-Mule cargo rover to instantly recalculate oxygen and kilocalorie burn. Developed as a lightweight, zero-dependency web app using HTML5, CSS3, Vanilla JavaScript (Canvas API), and a Python 3 server for simulated telemetry, ARES-HUD translates decades of robotic exploration into an actionable, life-saving tool for future crews
